learningObjective: Reason about tolerance choice when comparing an FP16-input FP32-accumulate matmul kernel against an FP32-input reference.

canonicalClaims.claim: For an FP16-input, FP32-accumulate GEMM compared to an FP32-input reference, expected relative error at K in the low thousands is on the order of 1e-3, dominated by FP16 input rounding (mantissa ~11 bits, relative epsilon ~9.77e-4). FP32 accumulation reduces but does not eliminate this input-precision loss.
conditions: Random inputs with typical range; no NaN/inf; standard tile schedule.
nonImplications: Does not imply the tolerance applies to FP8/INT8.
Does not imply modern GPU matmul is generally non-deterministic.

misconceptions.claim: FP32 accumulation guarantees bit-identical output to an FP32-input reference.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Input rounding to FP16 is the dominant error source; accumulation precision alone cannot recover it.

misconceptions.claim: GPU matmul is generally non-deterministic, so tolerance testing is meaningless.
misconceptions.whyWrong: For fixed algorithm/config, modern GPU matmul is deterministic; tolerance testing works.

misconceptions.claim: TF32 default in PyTorch always dominates errors when using `.float()`.
misconceptions.whyWrong: TF32 is used only for `matmul`/`conv` when enabled; and its effect depends on `torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32`.

misconceptions.claim: FP16 accumulation is safe up to K ~ 1e4.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FP16 accum error grows quickly with K; FP32 accum is preferred for K ≥ few hundred.

implementationFacts: Typical `torch.testing.assert_close` for FP16-input GEMM: rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-3.
